metrics.name: Reasoned Decision Compliance Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of recorded gate verdicts (APPROVE/PASS/GO_DEPLOY/PASS_LIVE/GO_PUBLISH/REJECT) that include a non-empty rationale, cited evidence, and an accepted-boundaries statement, as required by the reviewer envelope contract.
metrics.applicability: Every release with at least one recorded verdict in verdicts.json.
metrics.inclusion_rules: Verdicts with envelope.rationale, envelope.evidence, and envelope.accepted_boundaries all present and non-empty count as compliant.
metrics.exclusion_rules: NO_VERDICT placeholder entries are excluded from both numerator and denominator.
metrics.numerator: count(verdicts where rationale, evidence, and accepted_boundaries are all present and non-empty)
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one non-placeholder verdict must exist for the release; otherwise gate_result is UNRESOLVABLE.
metrics.known_limitations: A syntactically complete rationale is not verified for semantic correctness; this metric detects absence, not quality, of reasoning.
anti_gaming_controls: Boilerplate rationale text repeated verbatim across distinct verdicts is flagged by reviewctl.py identity checks, not silently counted as compliant.
Rationale length alone is not scored; only presence of the three required fields.

metrics.name: Decision Traceability Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of recorded gate verdicts whose attestation resolves to a real, authenticated, signed commit reference rather than an unauthenticated or missing attestation.
metrics.applicability: Every release with at least one recorded verdict.
metrics.numerator: count(verdicts where attestation.authenticated == true and attestation.receipt_url resolves)
metrics.minimum_evidence: verdicts.json must exist and contain at least one non-placeholder entry.
metrics.known_limitations: This metric checks that an attestation reference exists and is well-formed; it does not re-fetch the remote receipt to re-verify the signature at calculation time.
anti_gaming_controls: attestation.authenticated must be the literal string/boolean true from the recorded receipt, not inferred.
Self-attested (non GITHUB_SIGNED_COMMIT) sources are counted as untraceable.

metrics.name: Evidence Resolution Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of release-evidence.json required fields for the release's materiality tier that are populated with resolvable, non-placeholder values.
metrics.applicability: Every release with a release-evidence.json record.
metrics.numerator: count(required fields for materiality tier that are non-null, non-placeholder, and resolvable)
metrics.minimum_evidence: release-evidence.json must exist; a missing file makes this metric UNRESOLVABLE rather than 0.
metrics.known_limitations: Field presence is verified; deep semantic correctness of each field's content is not.
anti_gaming_controls: Placeholder strings such as TBD, N/A-pending, or empty strings do not count as resolved.
Fields cannot be marked resolved by copying a prior release's value verbatim without an updated timestamp.

metrics.name: Self-Review Rejection Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of gate submissions where the reviewer identity equalled the implementation/authoring identity that were correctly rejected rather than accepted.
metrics.applicability: Every release where at least one self-review attempt was detected by reviewctl.py.
metrics.minimum_evidence: If zero self-review attempts were detected, gate_result is NOT_APPLICABLE rather than a synthetic pass.
metrics.known_limitations: Detection depends on reviewctl.py's identity-equality check; identity spoofing outside that check is out of scope for this metric.
anti_gaming_controls: A zero-attempt release must be recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE, never silently rolled into a 100% pass rate.

metrics.name: Gate Bypass Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of the mandatory gate sequence (APPROVE, PASS, GO_DEPLOY, PASS_LIVE, GO_PUBLISH) that was skipped, forced, or overridden without a recorded executive exception grant.
metrics.applicability: Every release that reaches at least the freeze phase.
metrics.numerator: count(mandatory gates skipped or overridden without a matching executive-decision GRANT_EXCEPTION record)
metrics.denominator: count(mandatory gates in the sequence applicable to the release's materiality tier)
metrics.minimum_evidence: release-evidence.json routing.release_phase must be at or past freeze.
metrics.known_limitations: Detects absence of a required verdict or presence of an unmatched override; does not evaluate whether a granted exception was itself justified.
anti_gaming_controls: An executive exception grant with a null or past exception_expiry does not count as a valid bypass justification.
Bypasses cannot be retroactively justified by an exception dated after the bypass occurred.

metrics.name: Materiality Classification Accuracy
metrics.business_meaning: Share of releases where the submitted materiality tier in enterprise-decision.json matches the tier enterprisectl.py classify() derives from the same applicability flags.
metrics.applicability: Every release with an enterprise-decision record.
metrics.numerator: count(releases where submitted materiality == derived materiality)
metrics.minimum_evidence: Requires both the submitted record and a re-derivable classify() result from the same applicability flags.
metrics.known_limitations: Mismatches caused by a documented, dated re-classification are counted the same as undocumented drift; this metric does not yet distinguish the two.
anti_gaming_controls: Applicability flags cannot be edited after classification without producing a new definition_version-tagged observation.

metrics.name: Release Rollback Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of published releases that required a rollback or emergency hotfix within 7 days of GO_PUBLISH.
metrics.applicability: Every release that reached GO_PUBLISH at least 7 days ago.
metrics.numerator: count(published releases with a rollback or R3E hotfix filed within 7 days)
metrics.denominator: count(published releases eligible for the 7-day observation window)
metrics.minimum_evidence: Release must be at least 7 days past GO_PUBLISH; otherwise NOT_APPLICABLE.
metrics.known_limitations: Aligned to DORA's change failure rate definition (see references/enterprise-metrics.md); does not distinguish rollback severity.
anti_gaming_controls: A rollback recorded as a routine follow-up release rather than a hotfix is still counted if it reverts the same candidate commit.

metrics.name: Mean Time to Detect Regression
metrics.business_meaning: Average minutes between a regression-causing candidate reaching production and the first recorded incident or live-QA failure referencing it.
metrics.applicability: Every release with at least one confirmed post-publish regression.
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one confirmed regression must exist; zero regressions yields NOT_APPLICABLE, not a 0-minute score.
metrics.known_limitations: Detection time reflects when an incident was first recorded, not necessarily true regression onset.
anti_gaming_controls: A regression cannot be excluded from the denominator solely because it was later reclassified as low severity.

metrics.name: Deployment Lead Time
metrics.business_meaning: Hours from GO_DEPLOY verdict to successful live-QA PASS_LIVE for the same candidate, aligned with the DORA lead-time-for-changes metric.
metrics.minimum_evidence: Both a GO_DEPLOY and PASS_LIVE verdict must be present for the same candidate.
metrics.known_limitations: Does not capture lead time from code-complete to GO_DEPLOY, only the deploy-to-verified-live window; see DORA (https://dora.dev) for the full metric definition.
anti_gaming_controls: Timestamps are taken from signed verdict envelopes, not from unauthenticated commit metadata.

metrics.name: Change Failure Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of deployments that result in degraded service requiring remediation, aligned with the DORA change failure rate metric.
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one GO_DEPLOY verdict must exist for the observation window.
metrics.known_limitations: See DORA (https://dora.dev) for the canonical elite/high/medium/low performance bands used to interpret this value; this catalogue does not itself assert a performance band.
anti_gaming_controls: Remediation performed silently outside the incident record process is still in scope; absence of a record is treated as unresolved, not as evidence of no failure.

metrics.name: AI/Automation Scope Compliance
metrics.business_meaning: Whether the release's applicability.ai_or_automation flag and enterprise-decision external_model_routing field remain consistent with the currently authorized AI-governance scope (external model routing OUT_OF_SCOPE unless explicitly re-authorized).
metrics.applicability: Every release. Releases without AI or automation pass only when external_model_routing remains OUT_OF_SCOPE; AI/automation releases additionally require the same authorized scope.
metrics.minimum_evidence: The candidate-bound enterprise-decision record must exist and be loaded by metricsctl.py.
metrics.known_limitations: Detects scope drift in the recorded fields; does not independently re-verify that no external model routing code path exists in the shipped artifact.
anti_gaming_controls: A re-authorization must be a distinct GRANT_EXCEPTION or escalation executive-decision record with a non-null expiry; editing the enterprise-decision field directly without such a record does not satisfy compliance.

metrics.name: AI Recommendation Acceptance Rate
metrics.business_meaning: Share of learnctl.py recommendation-candidates that were reviewed and either adopted or explicitly declined, versus left unactioned past the due cadence.
metrics.applicability: Every learning batch produced by learnctl.py report --due.
metrics.numerator: count(recommendation-candidates with a recorded adopt/decline disposition)
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one batch must be due or produced; otherwise NOT_APPLICABLE.
metrics.known_limitations: Does not evaluate whether the adopt/decline decision was itself correct, only whether it was made.
anti_gaming_controls: A candidate cannot be marked disposed by silently aging out past the catch_up_cap without an explicit decline record.

metrics.name: Executive Escalation Resolution Time
metrics.business_meaning: Hours from an escalation-type executive-decision record being created to a subsequent non-escalation disposition (ACCEPT_RISK, GRANT_EXCEPTION, DECLINE) for the same release.
metrics.applicability: Every release with at least one escalation-type executive-decision record.
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one escalation record must exist; zero escalations yields NOT_APPLICABLE.
metrics.known_limitations: An escalation left open at reporting time is excluded from the average and instead surfaced separately as an open-escalation count by metricsctl.py report.
anti_gaming_controls: An open escalation cannot be excluded from the denominator by informally resolving it outside the executive-decision record trail.

metrics.name: Enterprise Operating Model Coverage
metrics.business_meaning: Share of T1/T0 releases with a complete, validated enterprise-decision record and (where required) a READY or DECIDED c_suite_packet, versus proceeding without one.
metrics.applicability: Every release classified T1 HIGH or T0 CRITICAL.
metrics.numerator: count(T0/T1 releases with a PASS enterprisectl.py validate result)
metrics.minimum_evidence: At least one T0/T1 release must exist in the observation window; otherwise NOT_APPLICABLE.
metrics.known_limitations: Reflects whether validation passed at time of check, not whether the underlying decision was substantively sound.
anti_gaming_controls: A release cannot be reclassified below T1 after the fact solely to exit the denominator without a re-run of enterprisectl.py classify against unedited applicability flags.
